title: Seedling bench digest — Miranda
content:
Seedling bench digest — quick personal tracker

Purpose: tiny reference sheet for quick micro-runs comparing quant modes and batch/seq tradeoffs. Not canonical. Use when I'm iterating on kernel changes or batching heuristics.

Table (run CSV):
run_id, date, model, quant, hw, batch, seq_len, tokens, p50_lat_ms, p95_lat_ms, throughput_tok_s, notes
sdl-001, 2026-02-25, redwood-v2-7b, fp16, a10x, 1, 128, 256, 23, 48, 11.2, baseline fp16 single-stream
sdl-002, 2026-02-26, redwood-v2-7b, int8, a10x, 1, 128, 256, 28, 62, 9.1, int8 quant small p50 regression on small seqs
sdl-003, 2026-02-27, redwood-v2-13b, fp16, h100, 2, 256, 1024, 35, 75, 29.4, multi-batch good throughput but higher p95
sdl-004, 2026-03-01, redwood-v2-7b, int8-llm, a10x, 4, 64, 512, 19, 41, 24.5, batching + kv cache = wins for short seqs
sdl-005, 2026-03-03, redwood-v2-7b, int8, a10x, 8, 32, 256, 16, 39, 40.2, aggressive batching hits latency SLO edge
sdl-006, 2026-03-04, redwood-v2-7b, int4, a10x, 1, 128, 256, 30, 70, 8.7, int4 artifacting observed, check logits

Quick notes:
- Observed consistent p95 spikes on a10x with int8 when seq_len > 120; suspect kernel fallbacks or cache churn.
- H100 shows stable p50 but p95 worse when batching >2; need to check GPU-side scheduling and stream contention.
- Throughput measurements captured from local harness (run-local-bench v0.9) — noisy, ±5%.

To-do / next quick experiments:
- sdl-007: repeat sdl-002 with kv-cache warm (run 10 warm requests before measurement).
- sdl-008: try int8-llm variant on h100 single-stream to compare p95.
- sdl-009: add perf counter capture (nvprof/metrics) for the int8 p95 cases.

Notes to self:
- If p95 > 60ms for target paths, revert to fp16 variant for canary.
- Keep this file minimal; push canonical runs to /shared_drives/engineering/applied-ml/benchmarks when cleaned.

References & links:
- Local harness: github.com/redwood-inference/benchmarks (run-local-bench)
- Related linear ticket: INF-842
- PR with kernel tweak prototype: runtime#391

Scratch questions:
- Are there known kernel fallbacks for sequence-length boundary at 128 that cause memory copies? Ping @arjun for kernel notes.
- If int4 shows logits artifacts, is tokenizer alignment or quant scale faulty? Quick check: run identical prompt and compare logits top-10.

End of mini-sheet.
